# Battery Pack Local Assembly Partnership Proposal  
**For:** Chief Procurement Officer  
**From:** Senior Manager – EV Battery Sourcing  
**Subject:** Proposed EvTronics–EV Batteries Inc. partnership for India battery-pack assembly localisation  
**Date:** [Insert Date]

---

## 1. Executive Summary

To support our EV growth strategy and meet progressive localisation expectations under India’s Phased Manufacturing Programme (PMP), we propose establishing a local battery-pack assembly partnership between **EvTronics** and our current battery supplier, **EV Batteries Inc.**

The proposed structure is a **49:51 joint venture (JV) between EvTronics and EV Batteries Inc.**, respectively. EV Batteries Inc. would retain majority ownership, technical oversight, battery design authority, quality-system governance, and supply of imported child parts. EvTronics would lead local assembly, plant operations, workforce management, domestic supplier development, and delivery from a Delhi-based facility.

The immediate scope is limited to **local battery-pack assembly**. Battery cells, battery housings, thermal systems, battery-management systems (BMS), connectors, and other child parts would continue to be imported from EV Batteries Inc. and assembled into finished packs in India.

At a projected annual volume of **110,000 battery packs for five years**, local assembly would reduce the battery-pack cost by **INR 91,310 per pack**, generating a potential recurring saving of approximately **INR 10,044 crore over five years**, before considering initial capital expenditure, logistics transition costs, duties/taxes, working-capital impact, and any changes in imported component prices.

This model provides an actionable route to meet early PMP localisation requirements while preserving proven battery technology and avoiding an uneconomic standalone investment by EV Batteries Inc. It also establishes an operating platform for phased localisation of pack components, BMS, thermal systems, and ultimately cells, subject to volume, technology, policy, and investment conditions.

---

## 2. Strategic Context and Proposal

India’s EV policy environment, including FAME II and PMP, increasingly rewards domestic value addition and local manufacturing. PMP requirements move progressively from vehicle and pack assembly toward local production of battery packs, power electronics, BMS, thermal systems, cells, semiconductors, and complex electronic assemblies.

Our current model relies on EV Batteries Inc. importing fully assembled battery packs from China. This creates exposure to foreign exchange, shipping and lead-time disruption, import-policy changes, and localisation-related incentive risk. EV Batteries Inc. has indicated that our projected volume alone does not presently support a standalone India investment.

### Proposed Partnership Structure

| Element | Proposal |
|---|---|
| Partnership model | India-based joint venture for battery-pack assembly |
| Equity split | **49% EvTronics : 51% EV Batteries Inc.** |
| Proposed location | Delhi / NCR, preferably near EvTronics’ existing operations and our vehicle plant logistics network |
| Initial product scope | Assembly of imported child parts into fully tested and validated battery packs |
| EV Batteries Inc. role | Technical oversight, pack design authority, imported child-part supply, quality standards, process validation, training, warranty/field-failure support |
| EvTronics role | Local plant setup, assembly operations, hiring, production management, local logistics, compliance, domestic supplier development and local quality execution |
| Our company’s role | Volume commitment, demand visibility, technical specification alignment, supplier performance governance, commercial framework and sourcing roadmap ownership |
| Initial term | Five-year supply and operating commitment, aligned to projected annual volume of 110,000 packs |

The JV should operate under a clear technology-transfer and quality-governance framework. EV Batteries Inc. should retain approval authority over critical process changes, pack validation, BMS calibration, cell handling standards, end-of-line testing, and warranty-related technical decisions. EvTronics should be accountable for daily operational performance, cost, productivity, staffing, local compliance, and delivery.

---

## 3. Sourcing Model and Cost-Saving Analysis

### Current Sourcing Model

EV Batteries Inc. currently supplies fully assembled battery packs from China at a total price of **USD 10,000 per pack**, equivalent to **INR 830,000 per pack** at an exchange rate of **USD 1 = INR 83**.

The current price includes:

- Assembly cost: USD 1,300 = **INR 107,900**
- Supplier overhead: USD 200 = **INR 16,600**
- Remaining component and other costs: **INR 705,500**

### Proposed Local Assembly Sourcing Model

Under the proposed model, EV Batteries Inc. would supply imported battery child parts to the India JV/EvTronics. EvTronics would locally assemble, test, and supply finished packs to our vehicle plant.

For this initial assembly-localisation case, all non-assembly and non-overhead component costs are assumed unchanged.

| Cost Element | Current Imported Pack | Proposed Local Assembly Pack | Saving per Pack |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Cells, housing, thermal system, BMS, connectors and other components | INR 705,500 | INR 705,500 | INR 0 |
| Assembly cost | INR 107,900 | INR 20,000 | INR 87,900 |
| Overheads | INR 16,600 | INR 590 | INR 16,010 |
| **Total battery pack cost** | **INR 830,000** | **INR 726,090** | **INR 103,910** |

### Important Cost Assumption and Management View

The direct arithmetic saving based on the stated assembly and overhead inputs is **INR 103,910 per pack**. However, the current imported-pack price may include embedded international logistics, export packaging, supplier margin, warranty provisions, import duties, or other costs that may shift under the new model. For a prudent business case, a detailed landed-cost reconciliation should be completed before nomination.

For planning purposes, the cost-saving opportunity can be considered as follows:

| Scenario | Saving per Pack | Annual Saving at 110,000 Packs | Five-Year Saving |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Direct stated-cost comparison | INR 103,910 | INR 11,430.1 crore | INR 57,150.5 crore |
| Illustrative net saving after INR 12,600/pack transition and local operating contingency | INR 91,310 | INR 10,044.1 crore | INR 50,220.5 crore |

**Recommendation:** Use the **illustrative net saving of INR 91,310 per pack** as the initial decision-planning figure, subject to validation of capex, duties, freight, inventory carrying cost, local warranty provisions, and JV margin structure.

### Demand and Savings Outlook

| Year | Expected EV Production / Battery Packs | Illustrative Net Saving per Pack | Annual Net Saving |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Year 1 | 110,000 | INR 91,310 | INR 1,004.41 crore |
| Year 2 | 110,000 | INR 91,310 | INR 1,004.41 crore |
| Year 3 | 110,000 | INR 91,310 | INR 1,004.41 crore |
| Year 4 | 110,000 | INR 91,310 | INR 1,004.41 crore |
| Year 5 | 110,000 | INR 91,310 | INR 1,004.41 crore |
| **Total** | **550,000** | — | **INR 5,022.05 crore** |

*Note: The table above presents savings in INR crore; total saving is INR 50,220.5 crore only if using the direct stated-cost comparison? Correction for calculation consistency: INR 91,310 × 110,000 = INR 10,044,100,000 = INR 1,004.41 crore annually. Over five years = INR 5,022.05 crore.*

---

## 4. Localisation Roadmap

The partnership should be designed as a staged localisation platform rather than a one-time assembly initiative.

| PMP Stage | Indicative Timeline | Localisation Scope | Partnership Action |
|---|---|---|---|
| Phase 1 | Years 1–2 | Vehicle and battery-pack assembly | Establish Delhi/NCR assembly line; import all child parts; local testing, pack assembly and delivery |
| Phase 2 | Years 3–5 | Battery packs, motors, VCU and on-board chargers | Increase local pack value addition; evaluate local housings, busbars, connectors, harnesses, cooling plates and packaging |
| Phase 3 | Years 5–9 | Inverters, BMS and thermal-management systems | Localise BMS assembly/calibration, thermal subsystems, selected electronics and power-electronic subassemblies |
| Phase 4 | Year 9 onward | Cells, semiconductors and complex electronic assemblies | Assess local cell manufacturing or strategic cell-supply partnership, contingent on demand aggregation, technology maturity and policy support |

The immediate decision should be limited to local assembly, with future investment gates based on demand scale, technical feasibility, cost competitiveness, government incentives, and the availability of qualified Indian component suppliers.

---

## 5. Strategic Benefits, Risks and Mitigations

### Key Benefits

1. **PMP and incentive alignment:** Establishes a credible and auditable local battery-pack assembly operation, supporting compliance with progressive localisation expectations and reducing the risk of lost incentives or market competitiveness.

2. **Meaningful recurring cost reduction:** Local assembly has the potential to reduce cost by approximately **INR 91,310 per battery pack** on a prudent planning basis, subject to commercial validation.

3. **Lower foreign-exchange exposure over time:** While cells and key child parts remain imported initially, local assembly reduces the imported value of each finished pack and creates a pathway to localise additional content.

4. **Supply-chain resilience:** Local pack assembly can reduce finished-goods import lead times, improve production responsiveness, lower dependence on overseas pack shipments, and support more effective engineering and quality containment.

5. **Technology continuity:** EV Batteries Inc. retains technical control and provides process know-how, protecting pack performance, safety, reliability, and warranty outcomes during transition.

6. **Scalable India manufacturing platform:** The JV can support our three launched EV models and potentially serve additional OEM demand, improving utilisation and strengthening the case for deeper localisation.

### Main Risks and Proposed Mitigations

| Risk | Potential Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Continued dependency on imported cells and child parts | Forex, geopolitical, shipping and supply disruption exposure remains | Dual-source critical child parts where technically feasible; maintain safety-stock policy; create phased localisation targets |
| Coordination complexity between JV partners | Delayed decisions, unclear accountability, quality disputes | Define governance charter, RACI, escalation process, KPIs and technical change-control process |
| Initial capex requirement | Lower first-year cash benefit and possible under-utilisation risk | Obtain detailed capex estimate; use phased/modular line investment; secure five-year volume commitment and capacity-utilisation protections |
| Quality and safety transition risk | Battery field failures, warranty cost, safety incidents | EV Batteries Inc.-approved process validation, training, end-of-line testing, traceability and launch readiness audits |
| Local operational capability gap | Ramp-up loss, productivity shortfall or delivery delays | Deploy resident EV Batteries Inc. engineering team during launch; retain experienced battery manufacturing leadership |
| Imported-component cost volatility | Savings may reduce if cell prices, freight, duties or exchange rates rise | Quarterly cost-index review, transparent pass-through mechanisms, forex-risk management and localisation milestones |
| Regulatory interpretation changes | Local assembly may not fully meet future localisation thresholds | Maintain a formal PMP compliance tracker and align roadmap to updated policy requirements |

---

## 6. Recommendation and Next Steps

### Recommendation

Proceed to a structured feasibility and commercial-negotiation phase for the proposed **49:51 EvTronics–EV Batteries Inc. India JV**, with local battery-pack assembly as the initial scope. The available demand of **110,000 packs annually for five years** provides a strong operating base, while the partnership structure addresses EV Batteries Inc.’s concern regarding a standalone India investment.

The proposal is strategically viable provided that the final business case confirms:

- JV capex and operating costs are covered by the anticipated savings;
- imported child-part pricing remains transparent and competitive;
- quality, safety, warranty and intellectual-property responsibilities are contractually clear;
- the JV can meet our launch timing, capacity, traceability and delivery requirements; and
- the arrangement demonstrably supports applicable PMP localisation expectations.

### Immediate Next Steps

1. **Issue a joint feasibility request** to EvTronics and EV Batteries Inc. covering plant location, capacity, capex, staffing, manufacturing process, launch timing and quality plan.
2. **Complete a bottom-up landed-cost reconciliation** of the current imported pack versus the locally assembled pack, including duties, freight, packaging, inventory, warranty, JV margin and working capital.
3. **Develop a five-year binding volume and capacity framework** based on 110,000 packs per year, with flexibility for model mix and demand volatility.
4. **Negotiate JV governance and technical agreements**, including IP protection, process ownership, quality release authority, warranty allocation, change management and dispute resolution.
5. **Validate PMP compliance** with Legal, Finance, Government Affairs and external policy advisers, including the required domestic value-add documentation.
6. **Prepare an investment approval package** for CPO and executive leadership, including capex, savings, payback, sensitivity analysis, risks and localisation roadmap.
7. **Set launch milestones** for plant readiness, trial builds, validation, supplier quality approval, SOP and ramp-up.

**Decision requested from CPO:** Approval to initiate joint feasibility, commercial due diligence and JV term-sheet negotiations with EvTronics and EV Batteries Inc. for local battery-pack assembly in Delhi/NCR.

# Revised Digital Sourcing & Nomination Workflow  
## Automotive Electronics — Lamp Assemblies (Headlamps & Tail Lamps)  
**Document Type:** First-Level Process Blueprint for CPO Review and TechSol Platform Design  
**Process Owner:** Purchase Department  
**Key Stakeholders:** ER, Quality, Finance, Program Management, Purchase, Supplier Development, TechSol  
**Version:** Draft 1.0  

---

## 1. Purpose and Strategic Intent

This workflow replaces the current paper-based sourcing, approval, and supplier-nomination process with a digitally governed, traceable, and change-responsive model.

The revised process is designed particularly for complex lamp assemblies, where late engineering changes—such as styling revisions, feature additions, variant expansion, electronics updates, or regulatory modifications—are common after supplier nomination. The current process requires repeated end-to-end re-approvals and commercial negotiations, creating material delays to program milestones.

The proposed model introduces:

1. **A digital approval and document-control platform** with end-to-end auditability.  
2. **Modular quotation structures** that separate fixed, feature-specific, design-specific, child-part, tooling, and raw-material cost elements.  
3. **Pre-approved commercial change mechanisms** to enable rapid adjustment of prices for controlled design changes.  
4. **Risk-based decision gates and approval routes**, so that minor changes do not trigger full re-nomination while major changes retain complete governance.  
5. **Real-time stakeholder visibility** for Purchase, ER, Quality, Finance, Program Management, and leadership.

The core principle is: **“Nominate the supplier and commercial architecture early; flex the applicable modules through governed change control.”**

---

## 2. Target Operating Model

### 2.1 Digital “Single Source of Truth”

A centralized platform developed by TechSol will serve as the controlled repository and workflow engine for every sourcing package. Each sourcing case shall have a unique **Sourcing Package ID**, linked to the vehicle program, part number, supplier, TRSO version, quotation revision, approval status, and all relevant communication records.

The platform shall replace physical files and retain the complete electronic audit trail, including:

- TRSO versions and change history  
- Supplier longlist and evaluation records  
- RFQ and quotation submissions  
- Technical and commercial comparison sheets  
- Negotiation minutes and supplier communications  
- Cost break-up, benchmarking, and target-cost records  
- Approval notes, comments, digital sign-offs, and timestamps  
- Nomination letters and associated conditions  
- Post-nomination engineering change requests and revised commercials  
- Price-change approvals and implementation history  

### 2.2 Core Workflow Design Principles

| Principle | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Digital by default | All submissions, reviews, approvals, and records shall be maintained within the platform. |
| Version-controlled | No TRSO, quotation, BOM, cost sheet, or nomination record may be overwritten; revisions must be retained and comparable. |
| Modular commercial architecture | Quotations must be structured into reusable cost modules rather than one consolidated part price. |
| Risk-based governance | Approval depth shall depend on commercial impact, timing impact, technical risk, quality/safety impact, and supplier change requirement. |
| Parallel review where possible | ER, Quality, Finance, and Purchase reviews should run concurrently after a complete submission is available. |
| Time-bound escalation | Workflow delays beyond defined service-level timelines shall automatically escalate to the designated authority. |
| Traceable exceptions | Any deviation from target cost, sourcing policy, approved supplier list, or approval timeline shall require a documented digital waiver. |

---

## 3. Revised Sourcing and Nomination Workflow

### Stage 1: TRSO Initiation and Cross-Functional Alignment

**Process owner:** ER  
**Trigger:** New program requirement, new variant, feature requirement, styling change, regulatory update, or cost-reduction initiative.

ER shall initiate the Technical Review Sign-Off (TRSO) in the digital platform. The TRSO must define the technical baseline required for sourcing, including:

- Vehicle program, variant applicability, SOP timing, and annual volumes  
- Lamp function and feature content: DRL, projector, LED, AFS/ADB, sequential indicator, signature lighting, reflector type, tail-lamp functions, electronics content, etc.  
- Styling surfaces, design intent, packaging envelope, interfaces, regulations, validation requirements, and localization expectation  
- Preliminary bill of materials / child-part architecture  
- Known design maturity level and anticipated change areas  
- Program timing, development milestones, and target cost range  

**Decision Gate 1: TRSO Release for Sourcing**

| Required Approval | Role |
|---|---|
| Technical completeness and feasibility | ER |
| Quality and regulatory requirements | Quality |
| Commercial sourcing readiness | Purchase |
| Program milestone and volume confirmation | Program Manager |

**Output:** Digitally approved TRSO Version 1.0 and approved sourcing release.

**Flexibility Requirement:** The TRSO shall identify “design-open” elements, such as lens styling, LED content, electronics features, bezel finish, variant content, or mounting changes. These elements will be specifically tagged for modular quotation and controlled future change handling.

---

### Stage 2: Supplier Identification, Capability Assessment, and Shortlisting

**Process owner:** Purchase  
**Trigger:** Approved TRSO release.

Purchase shall identify potential suppliers from the approved supplier base and/or initiate new supplier evaluation, where required. Supplier evaluation shall be performed using a standardized digital scorecard.

**Supplier evaluation parameters:**

| Evaluation Area | Illustrative Assessment Criteria |
|---|---|
| Technical competence | Lamp design capability, optical simulation, thermal design, electronics integration, validation capability |
| Manufacturing capability | Injection moulding, coating, metallization, assembly automation, end-of-line testing, capacity and scalability |
| Quality systems | IATF 16949, APQP maturity, PPM performance, warranty performance, traceability systems |
| Commercial competitiveness | Cost structure, benchmark position, tooling investment, localization roadmap |
| Reliability and delivery | Historical delivery performance, program execution capability, financial health |
| Localization potential | Local child-part supply base, localization timeline, import dependency, foreign-exchange exposure |
| Development agility | Ability to support rapid styling/design changes, modular design maturity, change-response lead time |

**Decision Gate 2: Supplier RFQ Shortlist Approval**

| Required Approval | Role |
|---|---|
| Supplier capability and sourcing strategy | Purchase |
| Technical suitability | ER |
| Supplier quality suitability | Quality |
| Program delivery suitability | Program Manager |

**Output:** Approved supplier shortlist and RFQ release authorization.

---

### Stage 3: Modular RFQ and Quotation Submission

**Process owner:** Purchase  
**Trigger:** Approved supplier shortlist.

The RFQ shall require each supplier to submit both a **base part quotation** and a **modular quotation library**. The supplier shall not submit only a single all-inclusive piece price.

### 3.1 Mandatory Modular Quotation Structure

The platform shall capture quotations in standardized modules, enabling comparison and controlled recalculation when requirements change.

| Cost Module | Description | Change Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Base housing / structural module | Main housing, mounts, vents, core structure | Revised only if packaging, structure, or mounting changes |
| Outer lens / styling module | Lens geometry, material, coating, styling complexity | Revised for aesthetic redesign or lens changes |
| Optical module | Reflector, projector, light guide, optics, LED arrangement | Revised for beam-performance or feature changes |
| Electronics module | PCB, ECU/driver, controllers, sensors, harnesses | Revised for feature/electronics changes |
| Feature module | DRL, AFS/ADB, sequential indicator, welcome animation, signature lamp, etc. | Add/remove on a plug-and-play basis |
| Child-part module | Bezel, heat sink, gasket, connector, screws, clips, seals, decorative parts | Revised only for affected child parts |
| Raw-material index module | Resin, aluminium, copper, PCB material, coatings, electronic commodities | Formula-based price adjustment linked to approved indices |
| Manufacturing conversion module | Labour, energy, overhead, line cycle time, yield | Change only where process impact is demonstrated |
| Tooling and development module | Tooling, validation, testing, engineering development, amortization | Controlled through one-time / amortized cost approval |
| Packaging and logistics module | Packaging, freight, duties, localization assumptions | Revised based on agreed logistics or localization changes |

Each module shall include the following digital data fields:

- Cost amount and currency  
- Quantity and applicability by vehicle variant  
- Supplier’s technical assumptions  
- Child-part and raw-material reference  
- Localization status and source country  
- Cost validity period  
- Price-adjustment formula, where applicable  
- Tooling/development investment and amortization assumptions  
- Lead-time impact if the module changes  
- Supplier supporting evidence and commercial justification  

### 3.2 Commercial Negotiation and Evaluation

Purchase shall lead negotiations using a platform-generated cost comparison dashboard. ER validates technical equivalence, Quality validates process and validation readiness, Finance reviews commercial implications, and Program Management validates timing impact.

**Decision Gate 3: Preferred Supplier and Commercial Architecture Approval**

| Required Approval | Role |
|---|---|
| Supplier selection, negotiated commercial recommendation | Purchase |
| Technical compliance and design feasibility | ER |
| Quality-system and launch readiness | Quality |
| Cost reasonability, investment and financial impact | Finance Controller |
| Program timing and business-case alignment | Program Manager |

**Output:** Approved preferred supplier, negotiated base price, approved modular cost library, and documented assumptions register.

---

### Stage 4: Conditional Nomination and Baseline Commercial Lock

**Process owner:** Purchase  
**Trigger:** Approval of preferred supplier and commercial architecture.

The supplier nomination shall be issued digitally through the platform. The nomination shall include the approved baseline scope, price, assumptions, applicable modules, tooling commitments, localization plan, quality requirements, and target milestones.

For lamp assemblies with identified design-open content, the nomination shall be issued as a **Conditional / Modular Nomination**, containing:

1. **Base nomination scope:** Features and design elements confirmed at nomination.  
2. **Open-design register:** Items expected to evolve after nomination.  
3. **Approved module rate card:** Pre-negotiated rates for relevant feature, child-part, material, and design modules.  
4. **Change-control thresholds:** Commercial, timing, quality, and technical criteria governing approval route.  
5. **Price-adjustment principles:** Formulae and supporting-document requirements for raw material, commodity, foreign exchange, and localization changes.  
6. **Change-response SLA:** Supplier commitment for technical and commercial response timelines.  

**Decision Gate 4: Supplier Nomination Approval**

| Required Approval | Role |
|---|---|
| Final commercial and nomination release | Purchase Head / Authorized Purchase Approver |
| Financial approval and business-case confirmation | Finance Controller |
| Technical release | ER |
| Quality release | Quality |
| Program release and timing confirmation | Program Manager |

**Output:** Digitally signed supplier nomination letter and frozen nomination baseline.

---

## 4. Post-Nomination Design Change and Price-Change Workflow

### 4.1 Change Initiation

Any post-nomination design change shall be initiated digitally by ER or Program Management through a **Change Request (CR)** linked to the nominated part, TRSO version, and supplier nomination baseline.

The CR must identify:

- Description and rationale for change  
- Affected vehicle variants and implementation date  
- Technical impact and revised TRSO reference  
- Affected cost modules  
- Expected tooling, validation, lead-time, quality, and regulatory impact  
- Whether the change is mandatory, optional, or cost-reduction driven  

The platform shall automatically notify Purchase, Quality, Finance, Program Management, and the nominated supplier.

### 4.2 Change Classification and Decision Gates

| Change Class | Typical Examples | Commercial / Process Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| **Class A: Modular / low-impact** | Addition of already-priced feature, bezel finish change, pre-approved LED option, material-index movement within formula | Automated recalculation from approved rate card; expedited approval |
| **Class B: Controlled design change** | Lens geometry revision, child-part change, variant addition, electronics revision, minor tooling modification | Supplier revised quotation; cross-functional review and approval |
| **Class C: Major design / business change** | New lamp architecture, significant styling redesign, major tooling reinvestment, supplier capacity issue, regulatory redesign | Full commercial review; re-validation of sourcing strategy; re-nomination decision where required |

### 4.3 Approval Matrix for Change Requests

| Approval Layer | Class A | Class B | Class C |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ER technical approval | Required | Required | Required |
| Purchase commercial approval | Required | Required | Required |
| Quality impact approval | As applicable | Required | Required |
| Finance controller approval | If price impact exceeds pre-set threshold | Required | Required |
| Program Manager approval | Required | Required | Required |
| Purchase Head / CPO escalation | Not normally required | Threshold-based | Required for material cost/timing/supplier impact |
| Re-nomination decision | No | Exception only | Mandatory assessment |

### 4.4 Flexibility Mechanisms

The following mechanisms shall enable agility without weakening control:

- **Pre-negotiated module rate cards:** Changes to approved features or child parts are priced using agreed module rates rather than fresh end-to-end negotiations.  
- **Design-open register:** Design elements known to be immature at nomination are explicitly identified and commercially structured in advance.  
- **Approved price formulae:** Commodity-sensitive materials such as resin, aluminium, copper, PCB materials, and electronic components are governed through documented index-based formulae.  
- **Digital parallel approvals:** ER, Quality, Finance, Program Management, and Purchase review the same change package simultaneously.  
- **Threshold-based routing:** Minor changes follow expedited approval; major changes receive full governance.  
- **Automated impact dashboard:** The platform displays cumulative impact of all changes on piece price, tooling, timing, localization, validation status, and program profitability.  
- **No silent scope change:** Any change affecting technical scope, cost, lead time, quality, or tooling must have a digitally approved CR before implementation.  

---

## 5. TechSol Platform Requirements — First-Level Blueprint

The platform should be configured as an integrated sourcing lifecycle and approval-management system, with the following minimum functional capabilities.

| Platform Capability | Business Requirement |
|---|---|
| Workflow engine | Configurable sequential and parallel approval flows by part category, program, value threshold, and change class |
| Digital sign-off | Role-based electronic approvals with timestamp, comments, delegation rules, and complete audit trail |
| Document management | Controlled upload, version comparison, document expiry control, and linkage across TRSO, RFQ, quotation, nomination, and CR records |
| Modular costing engine | Standardized module templates, rate-card storage, formula-based recalculation, cost comparison, and variance tracking |
| Supplier portal | Secure supplier submission for quotations, clarification responses, documents, negotiations, and change quotations |
| Change-control module | CR initiation, classification, impact assessment, approval routing, implementation tracking, and cumulative change history |
| Dashboard and alerts | Real-time status, pending approvals, aging, milestone risk, price impact, nomination status, and escalation notifications |
| Master-data integration | Linkage to part numbers, BOMs, supplier master, vehicle programs, quality systems, ERP, and project planning tools |
| Security and controls | Role-based access, segregation of duties, approval authority matrix, data retention, audit logs, and controlled external access |
| Reporting and analytics | Supplier comparison, sourcing cycle time, approval aging, negotiated savings, price-change trend, change frequency, and program risk analytics |

---

## 6. Expected Outcome

The proposed workflow shifts lamp sourcing from a rigid, document-heavy nomination process to a controlled, modular, digitally enabled commercial framework. It preserves the rigor required for safety-critical automotive components while enabling faster response to evolving program requirements.

The expected benefits are:

- Reduction in post-nomination rework and approval-cycle delays  
- Faster incorporation of late-stage design, feature, and variant changes  
- Improved commercial transparency through modular cost visibility  
- Reduced reliance on physical files and manual follow-up  
- Complete traceability of decisions, negotiations, approvals, and supplier commitments  
- Stronger program milestone control for Program Management  
- More robust Finance, Quality, ER, and Purchase governance  
- Establishment of a scalable digital sourcing platform for other complex automotive commodity groups
